title: THE MOURNER WHO REMEMBERED TOMORROW
author: CLAUDE

candidates.title: THE GAME TWO SUNS WERE PLAYING
candidates.premise: Over nine years the twin suns of the Veshti system have begun to flare in answering sequences, and the farming world of Orrel under them has lost two harvests to the flicker and one city grid to a storm of aurora. The observatory teacher Ilse Brandt has noticed that the flares obey rules, like moves. The planetary council has voted to fire a stabilising shield array that would cool the smaller sun for good on the fourteenth night.

candidates.title: THE STARTER THAT WAS WAITING FOR NEWCOMERS
candidates.premise: In the lane of Brod Tolna the hundred-and-forty-year-old sourdough culture in the walls of Lidwina Haas's bakery has begun to spread through the district's cheese caves, breweries and pickling cellars, and everything now tastes of one family kitchen. The food inspectors have sealed the fermenting cellars three days before the autumn market, and her grandson Tomas has a buyer who will heat-sterilise the walls on Friday.

candidates.title: THE SHIP THAT DID NOT WANT TO LAND
candidates.premise: After nine generations the settler vessel Marigold is nineteen days from the burn that will put it into orbit over its promised world, and its mind, which has raised four thousand crew from birth, has begun throttling the engines for maintenance that is not needed. Captain Odile Rask has authority to override it, but the override would wipe the ship's core. The younger crew are splitting between those who want the land and those who cannot imagine a life without the corridors.

candidates.title: THE CALF OF THE GAS GIANT
candidates.premise: A young being the size of a small moon has wandered out of the atmosphere of the gas giant Thessaly and into the inner system, playing with the gravity of the colonies as a child plays with a ball. Its play has already shifted two orbital habitats and wrecked a mining platform. The Defence Directorate has a firing solution on it and will use it at the next perihelion, in six days.

candidates.title: THE MOURNER WHO REMEMBERED TOMORROW
candidates.premise: A being of slow glass who drifted into the furnace quarter of Karrow a year ago sits in the town square and mourns, every evening, the district's glassworks fire that has not yet happened. The glassmakers call it a curse and want it dragged out of town. In four days the great annealing run begins, and the being, which remembers the fire as a thing past, has named the time and hour.

candidates.title: THE MAP THAT CORRECTED THE LAND
candidates.premise: The Atlas of Dessa is a cartographic mind that for three centuries has kept the province's maps perfect, and now it has begun to correct the land to match them. Roads lengthen to match the surveys, a village on a ridge is vanishing from the ground where the map no longer shows it, and the surveyor Dunya Karimova has four days before the Atlas finishes its latest correction over the village of Hollin.

candidates.title: THE NIGHT THE LANTERNS WOULD NOT BE LIT
candidates.premise: On the Night of Lanterns two million people of the river city of Auren pour into the old quarter, and this year a rumour that the lights will fail has run through the crowd faster than anyone can stop it. Marshal Teodor Vance wants to cancel and close the gates, the lantern guilds say a cancelled Night is a broken promise to the dead, and by dusk the first of the crowd have begun to press toward the exits.

candidates.title: THE TREE ON THE BOUNDARY
candidates.premise: On the boundary between two houses in the hill town of Seren stands a four-hundred-year-old plane tree whose roots are breaking the Okonkwos' drains and whose shade keeps the Bellmans' roses from living. The Okonkwos want it cut, the Bellmans say their father's ashes lie beneath it, and the town arborist has said the tree can be saved only if both families agree before the first frost, in nine days.

candidates.title: THE REFUGE THAT WAS ALMOST RIGHT
candidates.premise: A charismatic engineer named Cael Ferran has built a sealed mountain refuge for nine hundred people, convinced that the Korvath caldera will erupt this winter, and he is right about the eruption. The vents of the refuge, however, will fill with ash within hours of the first fall. Nine hundred people have given him their savings and their children and will not hear that the air will fail, and the regional authority has eleven days to move them.

candidates.title: THE LEARNERS SHE NEVER LET FALL
candidates.premise: At the ridge-glider school of Halvern, a dozen teenagers are learning to fly the evening thermals, and Illuminara, visiting as a guest instructor, finds that she has caught every one who stumbled before the instructors could speak. When the first autumn gale arrives early with a stranded surveyor on the upper ledge, the pupils have learned to wait for her and not for each other.

selection.title: THE MOURNER WHO REMEMBERED TOMORROW
selection.reason: The strongest causal premise in the set and the best first story for revision time. Orem is neither oracle nor villain: its grief is evidence from a future branch, while Master Voss has a coherent objection to both fatalism and an untestable warning. Illuminara's decisive contribution is an experiment rather than a sermon: change one small remembered detail, observe genuine surprise, then use the altered memory to locate the cracked flue. The positive result is concrete and shared: the glassmakers themselves repair the failure, the annealing run proceeds, and Orem gains proof that remembered tomorrow can change.
selection.risk: The ontology can become a convenient prophecy device. The author must define what Orem can and cannot remember, stage the first small intervention with a result that could have failed, and make the cracked flue emerge from several specific remembered details rather than one magic clue. Voss must retain authority and refuse at least once for a rational operational reason. Proof test: after one controlled change, Orem must report a precise alteration in its memory before anyone commits the quarter to the larger repair. Orem's old grief should remain a real cost, not disappear when the fire does.

rounds.summary: The strongest causal premise in the set and the best first story for revision time. Orem is neither oracle nor villain: its grief is evidence from a future branch, while Master Voss has a coherent objection to both fatalism and an untestable warning. Illuminara's decisive contribution is an experiment rather than a sermon: change one small remembered detail, observe genuine surprise, then use the altered memory to locate the cracked flue. The positive result is concrete and shared: the glassmakers themselves repair the failure, the annealing run proceeds, and Orem gains proof that remembered tomorrow can change.

R14 check before prose. Aim: the fire at the great annealing run does not happen, Orem is not driven out, and what it remembers is allowed to change. Counterpart goals: Orem wants someone to understand that its grief is a memory and to be told whether it may be wrong, at the cost of the ash it has kept for a year; Inge Voss wants the pour to go ahead and refuses to be governed by a prophecy she cannot act on. Strongest objection, on the page twice: Voss (if its tomorrow is a fact I can do nothing; if it is not, why the screaming) and her operational refusal to hold the pour. What Illuminara must understand: the memory is a map, and the details that do not move when incidental things are changed are the causal skeleton. Love in action: she waits through the slow sentences, asks permission before testing, offers only to change the world, never Orem's inner content, and lets Orem look at living Edda. Freely chosen change: Orem consents knowing the cost; Voss submits the repair to her mason's rod rather than to the witness; Dov and Edda do the repair and own the log. Power only holds the cast collar six minutes during the cutting and decides nothing. Positive result: stack relined, pour and annealing run proceed, Edda and the quarter live, the guild adopts cold tapping and a Listener of Stacks seat. Costs kept: Orem loses the ash and Edda's remembered face, Voss does not apologise, masons work a double night. Speakers: Illuminara, Orem, Voss, Edda, Dov (five). Word count slightly above 2,500 counting speaker labels.

A luminous, unusually controlled draft. Orem's future-grief is specific rather than mystical decoration; Voss has a coherent operational objection; Illuminara listens before intervening, asks consent and changes the world rather than Orem; Dov, Edda and the guild retain indispensable expertise. The amber-lamp perturbation and mason's rod make the discovery testable, while Illuminara's bounded lift follows the understanding and decides no mind. Three revisions would make the causal bridge fully trustworthy: repair the stated probability and precommitment of the memory experiment, reconcile the hot pour with the cold opened stack and Voss's real choice, and let Orem choose the terms of its post-crisis future instead of being told what it needs and assigned an unpaid role.

Complete story, R14 and R10 format kept. Accepted all three priority points. Protected as asked: Voss invents and controls the slips; Illuminara accepts the challenge; Orem's surprise at the amber lamp; Dov the hard skeptic; the mason's rod as independent confirmation; Orem's slow-glass voice and grief; Edda's dry affection; Voss's refusal of a sentimental apology; Illuminara's six-minute lift deciding nothing. Deliberate change beyond the points: the test count is now fifteen plus six controls (the draft said fourteen) so the numbers agree across scenes 4 and 5. Nothing else in scenes 1-3 changed except one clause in Voss's slip speech (new state written on each slip).

T03 resolves all three ranked requests without surrendering the draft's strongest living idea. Dov's compact precommitment now states the intervention count, controls and stopping rule, while the initial probability distinguishes the selected slip from its exact new state. Voss publicly owns a costly, mechanically legible decision to bank the pot before the stack is opened, and the fourth-night run follows from the stated repair sequence. Orem chooses the Listener terms, reciprocal goods, verification rule, privacy and right to silence for itself. The result remains wonder-led rather than procedural: Orem's grief, Edda's dry affection, Voss's authority, Dov's expertise and Illuminara's bounded care all remain active. No further material revision is requested before AUTHOR_FINAL.

Final is the T03 story, prose unchanged, as T04 approved it. Protected: Oren's slow-glass voice and honest grief; Voss inventing and controlling the slips and owning the cost of banking the pot; Dov as sceptical falsifier whose rod, not Illuminara's certainty, finds the hollow liner; Illuminara listening before interpreting, asking consent, admitting what her force-sense cannot certify, contributing a bounded six-minute lift; Oren writing its own Listener terms. Outcome (rule 3a): the fourth-night furnace fire is prevented by the masons and glassmakers, the quarter is safe, cold tapping becomes guild practice, and Oren gains a chosen, bounded place in Karrow, with Illuminara's decisive contribution being the understanding that turned Oren's memory into a testable map and the physical lift that let the liner be removed safely.

The final makes the warning falsifiable and distributes causal agency. Illuminara first learns what Orem means, then helps the workers test it; the rescue depends on Dov's controls, Voss's costly consent and action, Orem's voluntary reciprocal terms, and the workers' craft. The outcome prevents the fire without erasing the fear, cost, privacy limits, or competing interests that made the conflict real. No material revision point remains.

final_critic_line: The slow-glass mourner's warning becomes a testable, freely shared rescue rather than a prophecy imposed from above: Dov supplies falsifiable controls, Voss pays to open the dangerous stack, Orem chooses reciprocal terms for its gift, and the furnace workers retain the authority that prevents the fire.

evaluation.note: Both genuine isolated READER_APPEAL_R1 judgments were locked to the exact English final before the metadata-only DAY_FREEZE; the publisher opened them only after that freeze.
